caption: well little did I know I wasn’t being loyal to myself 🧚🏽‍♂️ we’re going where the wind takes us this summer. Bc what do you mean I am living my dream life and holding myself back bc of “oh I wanna treat people how I wanna be treated” nah girl I need to treat myself how I wanna be treated and that’s by staying loyal to what I want and desire!
author: aya shelbs l dallas | wellness | lifestyle  🧚‍♂️
transcript: I am not saying I want more dick or I want to kiss more people, however, I am realizing that I've never really had a slut girl summer and I am living like I am 75 with a man and children. I am loyal to people that do not deserve my loyalty because what I am essentially doing is abandoning myself and what I really want and the experience that I really want because I have this idea of like I'm going to treat people how I want to be treated but ultimately with that mindset, I'm forgetting everything that I actually want because I'm afraid that I'm going to hurt the other person because I don't want to hurt the other person but I'm hurting myself. Babes! At 19, I got in a relationship for 8 years, got married, after my divorce, I started traveling and I was so heartbroken that I didn't even really get to enjoy my life. I am now 30, living in the Caribbean, working for myself, single, no children, what? Let it run it back, let it run it back, like I just need to be more in the moment, I need to be more selfish and I'm realizing that like this is...
title: Choosing Yourself Over Loyalty to Others
one_liner: After years of prioritizing others, she's reclaiming her desires and choosing radical self-loyalty at 30.
key_points: Treating others how you want to be treated can mean abandoning your own wants and needs
Staying loyal to undeserving people is a form of self-abandonment
After an 8-year marriage and heartbreak, she's choosing to be present and selfish with her own life
Being 'in the moment' and prioritizing personal desire is reframed as self-respect, not selfishness
